events.title: James Joyce Walking Tour
events.description: A fun and exciting walking tour of James Joyce's Dublin offered by the James Joyce Centre. Though Joyce lived most of his life outside of Ireland, Dublin would provide the backdrop for virtually all of his work. On a stroll around the inner city, our guide will explain the real-life inspiration behind some of Joyce’s most celebrated writing, demonstrating just how central the streetscape of the ‘Hibernian metropolis’ was to the author’s life and art. The tour visits such stops as Belvedere College, the Gresham Hotel, the James Joyce Statue, Davy Byrnes, and the National Library. This is an excellent and fun introduction to Joyce in a bustling part of the city. Every Thur, Fri & Sat at 11am. Admission to the James Joyce Centre is included.

This unique programme of funded, artist-initiated projects selected via open call is highly accessible to artists, with a focus on early career, emerging artists and recent graduates. Projects are supplemented with artists' talks, texts, workshops or performances, and gallery visits by colleges and local schools.

events.title: Dublin by Dusk
events.description: Dublin by Dusk invites locals and visitors to enjoy the city centre in a new way on the last Thursday of each month. Participating venues and businesses will bring their own flavour to the evening, from late openings, tours and pop-up activities to cultural experiences, food and drink offers, shopping promotions and family-friendly options. It is a city-wide invitation to stay a little longer, discover something new and enjoy Dublin’s evening atmosphere across culture, hospitality, retail and visitor attractions. The programme is supported by the Department of Culture, Communications and Sport, Dublin City Council, Fáilte Ireland and Dublin Town, working together with businesses and cultural partners to further re-energise the city centre.

events.description: Step into the darker, more powerful world of Irish mythology through this live storytelling performance. Performed entirely from memory, this intimate one-man theatrical show brings Ireland’s legendary heroes, warriors and ancient tales to vivid life. Audiences experience stories of heroism, passion, violence and fate as they were originally told long before they were softened for modern audiences. Designed for mature audiences, this is a unique cultural experience that offers visitors a deeper, more memorable encounter with Irish mythology and storytelling tradition. events.title: Rembrandt to Matisse – A Celebration of European Works on Paper
events.description: Drawings, prints, watercolours and photographs by a range of European artists from the fifteenth century to the present day are included. The exhibition explores the diverse subjects and styles that have shaped European art through the centuries. Reflecting shifts in taste and technique over the centuries, the exhibition showcases the strength of the Gallery’s collection across the various schools. Curator: Niamh MacNally, Curator of the Prints and Drawings Study Room at the National Gallery of Ireland. events.title: 'Thinning the Veil': Art Exhibition
events.description: Six contemporary Fingal artists come together at Malahide Castle this autumn in an exhibition exploring memory, history, heritage and the changing role of monuments in contemporary Ireland. Curated by Eamonn Maxwell, the exhibition features sculptures, installations, sound works and graphic pieces throughout the castle. From 22 September, the programme continues with free special events including a Curator’s Tour & Artist Q&A with Eamonn Maxwell and Deborah Hewson, artist talks and exhibition tours with Ann Ensor, Laura Skehan, Michelle Hall and Susan Buttner, a live performance by Tadhg Kinsella, and a closing night exhibition tour with Cathal Dowd Smith. events.title: Come Fly With Me: Aviation, Tourism and Irish Design
events.description: Our current exhibition at the National Print Museum, Come Fly With Me: Aviation, Tourism and Irish Design, uses flight as a central thread to explore how design and print helped promote Irish modernisation and position Ireland internationally. With the arrival of a number of Dutch graphic designers to Ireland in the 1950s to work on advertising for Aer Lingus, depictions of Ireland and Irishness were forever changed, as was Ireland’s relationship to Continental Europe and the US. Their design work was recognised internationally and had a huge impact on Irish design and economic development. Free admission. Readers are advised to check with the venue before relying on the details published here.

Visitors can explore at their own pace after work, avoid daytime crowds, and enjoy a different atmosphere in the city's historic Docklands. A museum as tailored for locals as it is for tourists, if you've never visited EPIC, let this be your sign. events.title: Willy Russell’s Shirley Valentine
events.description: Meet Shirley, a 45-year-old housewife, trapped in a dreary marriage and humdrum life. As she prepares her husband’s dinner - egg and chips - Shirley wonders when she lost her hopeful, youthful self. Feeling isolated, she resorts to full-blown (although somewhat one-sided) conversations with her bestie – her kitchen wall and dreams of excitement beyond her grim role as “St. Joan of the fitted units". So, when an unexpected chance to travel to Greece appears, Shirley takes a leap, digs deep into her flagging confidence and discovers it’s never too late to reclaim your dreams, your joy, and yourself. The production promises laughter, poignancy, and an unforgettable evening with one of theatre’s most iconic characters. events.title: Long Day's Journey by Pan Pan
events.description: Pan Pan return to the stage with Long Day’s Journey – a play which conjures the atmosphere of a whistling morgue offering a theatrical hallucination of gritty family prone issues. The show makes its world premiere at Project Arts Centre, this November. Inspired by legendary American playwright Eugene O’Neill’s original play, A Long Day’s Journey Into Night, Pan Pan’s new interpretation, Long Day’s Journey, travels further into the sub-conscious hallucinatory world of O’Neill’s original work that spotlights themes of addiction, depression and despair. O'Neill’s poetically titled plays were among the first to introduce into the U.S., drama techniques of realism, earlier associated with Chekhov, Ibsen, and Strindberg.

events.title: Remembering World War 1 Tour
events.description: Join us at the GPO Museum for this special tour as we remember those involved in World War 1. In September 1914 Europe went over the precipice and war was declared. The people of the island of Ireland were faced with stark choices; join the war effort and support the British Empire, or take the opportunity the war provided to fight for the Ireland they wanted. This guided tour will tell the stories of those Irishmen and women who participated in World War 1, both their actions during the war and their lives afterwards, the effect and role the Irish Revolution had on these individuals, and how they are remembered today, not just in Ireland but in the countries they fought in across Europe.

events.title: Jason Byrne – 30 Years Byrning
events.description: Thirty years of stand-up. Thousands of shows. Millions of laughs. Now Jason Byrne is celebrating it all with “30 Years Byrning”. In this, his most ambitious show yet, Jason revisits fan favourite stunts and reveals what really happened along the way. Expect the usual, but of course expect the unusual. It’s Jason Byrne, he’s going to sum up 30 years and 30 shows in one glorious fun filled show. This could be the crowning achievement from “The Outright King Of Live Comedy”. Can Jason make sense of the nonsense. You really won’t want to miss him trying.
